issue.title: bob capture swallows unknown flags as task text, so Bob Mac Capture's --require-pull-in-choice fallback can never fire

task_type_fields.impact: Low frequency (Bryan normally updates bob and the app together), but the failure mode is silent vault corruption: a junk inbox task holding the flag text and the entire draft, reported to the app as a successful capture. Any future internal capture flag shares the hazard; the saved-templates epic plans an identity gate for `--template-origin` for exactly this reason. Fix options: gate the guard flag on a positive capability bob already advertises (for example `pull_in.supported` from a preview of the same executable identity) and delete the dead fallback, or have bob refuse unknown `--long` options that appear before `--`.
task_type_fields.repro:
Against a throwaway vault (`BOB_DIR` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` set to a temp dir, `mac_inbox.md` present), with today's bob (`~/.cargo/bin/bob`, bob-cli master `ca88db38`):

```bash
bob capture --format json --require-pull-in-choice-x -- hi; echo "exit=$?"
# {"ok":true,"dry_run":false,...,"text":"--require-pull-in-choice-x -- hi",
#  "task_line":"- [ ] #task --require-pull-in-choice-x -- hi [created::2026-10-16]",...}
# exit=0
```

`bob capture`'s `TEXT` positional is `trailing_var_arg(true)` plus `allow_hyphen_values(true)` (`src/native/capture/cli.rs` `text_arg`), so an unknown `--flag` in Bob Mac Capture's argv order (`capture --format json <flag> -- <draft>`) becomes the start of TEXT: bob captures the flag, the `--`, and the whole draft as one task and exits 0. No "unexpected argument" error is ever printed.

`BobProcessClient.capture` sends `--require-pull-in-choice` and relies on `isUnsupportedGuardFlagFailure` (exit 2 + "unexpected argument '--require-pull-in-choice'") to fall back for an older bob. That branch can never fire for `bob capture`, so an older bob without the guard flag writes a garbage task containing the draft instead of falling back.

issue.creation_reason: While planning saved capture templates, a probe showed that an older bob captures unknown capture flags as task text instead of erroring, which makes the Mac app's existing --require-pull-in-choice fallback dead code and leaves a silent vault-corruption path.

payload.entry: bob-cli-8b.land: bob-cli-8b hit the same root cause for the hidden --template-origin flag and worked around it in the Mac app only: BobProcessClient sends --template-origin only after a capture-templates list from the same executable identityToken succeeded (bob-mac-capture Sources/CaptureCore/BobProcessClient.swift ~298-310, 403-409). That identity gate is a precedent for --require-pull-in-choice; a bob-side fix for unknown-flag swallowing would make both gates unnecessary.

payload.description: Lander bob-cli-an.6.6: rank candidates for the batch-4 successor epic

payload.entry: Verified on this tree after the short-cluster walker in src/native/capture_flag_guard.rs. consume_short_cluster walks mixed switch+value clusters (-nf json, -nfjson, equals-only -c combined with another declared short) and then sees --bogus. Unknown alphabetic long flags in option position exit 2 with the clap unexpected-argument error (JSON via --format json). Isolated-vault probes leave the inbox and capture-templates shelf unchanged. Integration cargo test --test cli capture::flag_guard: 9 passed, including capture-complete --cursor 0 --format json --bogus. Unit tests include mixed clusters, attached-value TEXT on -fn json, undeclared cluster TEXT, and guard_specs_match_clap_declarations against build_cli(). just check green (cargo fmt --check, clippy -D unused, CLI suites). Decision capture_flag_guard=refuse honored. Mac pull-in argv tests now omit --require-pull-in-choice unless a same-executable preview had pull_in.supported; guard-refusal first obtains a capability-bearing no-offer preview then a write-only refusal via FAKE_BOB_CAPTURE_WRITE_STDOUT. just portable-check 1555/0. Known b7 RefsLibraryTests remain out of scope.
